\begin{definition}[Total influence]
\lean{FABL.totalInfluence}
\statementsource{lmn-constant-depth-fourier}{pdf-63759bd909d5-p011-b006}
\statementsource{Analysis-of-Boolean-Functions-by-Ryan-ODonnell}{
  pdf-ffbe9c7b3306-p049-b005,
  pdf-ffbe9c7b3306-p213-b005,
  pdf-ffbe9c7b3306-p267-b001,
  pdf-ffbe9c7b3306-p267-b005
}
\statementsource{mossel-neeman-gaussian-noise-stability}{pdf-b53c1a5aa27d-p007-b003}
\label{FABL.totalInfluence}
\leanok
\uses{FABL.influence}
For a real-valued function $f$ on the $n$-dimensional sign cube, its total influence is
the sum of its coordinate influences.
\end{definition}

\begin{theorem}[Nonnegativity of total influence]
\lean{FABL.totalInfluence_nonneg}
\label{FABL.totalInfluence_nonneg}
\leanok
\uses{FABL.influence_nonneg, FABL.totalInfluence}
\difficulty{1}
For every real-valued function $f$ on a finite-dimensional Boolean cube, its total
influence is nonnegative.
\end{theorem}

  {direct}
  {Analysis-of-Boolean-Functions-by-Ryan-ODonnell}
  {pdf-ffbe9c7b3306-p049-b005}
\difficulty{3}
For every natural number $n$ and every real-valued function $f$ on $\{-1,1\}^n$, its
total influence is the uniform expectation of the sum of the squares of its coordinate
discrete derivatives:
$\operatorname{Inf}_{\mathrm{tot}}(f)=\mathbb{E}_{x\sim\mathrm{Unif}(\{-1,1\}^n)}\sum_{i=1}^n
(\partial_i f(x))^2$.
\end{theorem}

\begin{definition}[Pointwise sensitivity]
\lean{FABL.sensitivity}
\statementsource{lmn-constant-depth-fourier}{pdf-63759bd909d5-p011-b006}
\statementsource{Analysis-of-Boolean-Functions-by-Ryan-ODonnell}{pdf-ffbe9c7b3306-p017-b008}
\statementsource{mossel-neeman-gaussian-noise-stability}{pdf-b53c1a5aa27d-p007-b003}
\label{FABL.sensitivity}
\leanok
\uses{FABL.BooleanFunction, FABL.IsPivotal}
Let $f$ be a Boolean function on the $n$-dimensional sign cube, and let $x$ be an input.
The sensitivity of $f$ at $x$ is the number of coordinates that are pivotal for $f$ at
$x$.
\end{definition}

\begin{theorem}[Sensitivity as a sum of pivotal indicators]
\lean{FABL.sensitivity_cast_eq_sum_pivotalIndicator}
\label{FABL.sensitivity_cast_eq_sum_pivotalIndicator}
\leanok
\uses{FABL.BooleanFunction, FABL.pivotalIndicator, FABL.sensitivity}
\difficulty{1}
Let $f:\{-1,1\}^n\to\{-1,1\}$ be a Boolean function and let $x\in\{-1,1\}^n$. The number
of coordinates whose sign flip changes $f(x)$ equals the sum, over all coordinates, of
the indicator that the coordinate is pivotal at $x$.
\end{theorem}

\begin{definition}[Average boundary edge fraction]
\lean{FABL.boundaryEdgeFraction}
\statementsource{Analysis-of-Boolean-Functions-by-Ryan-ODonnell}{
  pdf-ffbe9c7b3306-p046-b004,
  pdf-ffbe9c7b3306-p050-b002
}
\label{FABL.boundaryEdgeFraction}
\leanok
\uses{FABL.BooleanFunction, FABL.dimensionEdgeBoundaryFraction}
For a Boolean function $f$ on the $n$-dimensional sign cube, its boundary edge fraction
is the sum, over all coordinates, of the dimension-wise edge boundary fractions, divided
by $n$.
\end{definition}

\begin{theorem}[Boundary edge fraction eq total influence div]

\begin{definition}[Undirected cube edges]
\lean{FABL.UndirectedCubeEdge}
\label{FABL.UndirectedCubeEdge}
\leanok
\uses{FABL.DimensionEdge}
For a natural number $n$ and a coordinate $i\in\{0,\ldots,n-1\}$, let a dimension edge
in direction $i$ be an edge of the Boolean cube that changes only coordinate $i$. The
set of undirected cube edges is the set of pairs consisting of a coordinate $i$ and a
dimension edge in direction $i$.
\end{definition}

\begin{definition}[Undirected cube boundary fraction]
\lean{FABL.undirectedCubeBoundaryFraction}
\label{FABL.undirectedCubeBoundaryFraction}
\leanok
\uses{FABL.BooleanFunction, FABL.IsBoundaryDimensionEdge, FABL.UndirectedCubeEdge, FABL.allOneDimensionEdge, FABL.uniformProbability}
Let $n>0$ and let $f$ be a Boolean function on the $n$-dimensional cube with values in
$\{\pm1\}$. The undirected cube boundary fraction of $f$ is the probability that a
uniformly chosen undirected cube edge has endpoints on which $f$ takes different values.
\end{definition}

  {pdf-ffbe9c7b3306-p050-b002}
\difficulty{4}
Let $n>0$ and let $f:\{-1,1\}^n\to\{-1,1\}$. Choose uniformly an undirected edge of the
$n$-dimensional cube, and let the boundary fraction be the probability that the
endpoints receive different values under $f$. Then this fraction equals the total
influence of $f$, defined as the sum over coordinates of the uniform average of the
squared discrete derivative, divided by $n$.
\end{theorem}

\begin{theorem}[Square of a sign monomial]
\lean{FABL.monomial_sq}
\label{FABL.monomial_sq}
\leanok
\uses{FABL.monomial, FABL.signValue, FABL.signValue_eq_neg_one_or_one}
\difficulty{4}
For every nonnegative integer $n$, every subset $S$ of the $n$ coordinates, and every
sign vector $x\in\{\pm1\}^n$, the square of the monomial indexed by $S$ at $x$ is $1$.
\end{theorem}

\difficulty{3}
For every $n\ge 0$, let the sign-valued OR function on the $n$-dimensional Boolean cube
equal $1$ when every coordinate is $1$, and equal $-1$ otherwise. Its total influence is
$n/2^{n-1}$.
\end{theorem}

\difficulty{3}
For every natural number $m$, the total influence of majority on $2m+1$ sign coordinates
is $\displaystyle (2m+1)\frac{\binom{2m}{m}}{2^{2m}}$.
\end{theorem}
